newsitem.title: USA: Coke's Surge aims to turn Pepsi green.
newsitem.headline: Coke's Surge aims to turn Pepsi green.

text.p: Armed with new green soda Surge and gunning for teen drinkers, Coca-Cola Co is mounting a late but direct challenge to one of PepsiCo Inc's powerhouses, Mountain Dew.

"This is a chance to attack the archenemy. Coke has had spectacular results with Sprite, clobbering 7-UP, and now it's going for Mountain Dew, which is one of the pillars that holds up Pepsi," said Tom Pirko of industry consulting firm Bevmark.

Coke shares rose 5/8 to 48-1/2 after it announced aggressive launch plans for the new drink, including advertisements during the Super Bowl and about five million free samples. Pepsi shareholders were apparently unfazed by the news, with the stock rising 1/4 to 29-3/8.
Surge is a bright green-colored soda with a wider mouth for easier drinking, less carbonation, and maltodextrin, an energy-yielding complex carbohydrate.
7-UP is made by Cadbury Schweppes Plc.

Coke said it is aiming the drink at the "Clueless" crowd of adolescents and teenagers, named for the popular movie, who are a few years younger than "Generation X" and have been guzzling Mountain Dew in droves.

Mountain Dew had 1995 sales of about $2.7 billion and a market share of about five percent. Its campaigns have included "in your face" and "Do the Dew" youth-oriented slogans and promotion using beepers.

"Mountain Dew is exposed because of its demographics. Young teens are very vulnerable to advertising. They drink a lot and are highly active so you can tie in many other things besides taste. They are a perfect market, so all Coke's guns are pointed there," he said.
"Mountain Dew is the number two brand at Pepsi and one of the brightest spots in its North American business. It was the fastest growing brand until Sprite pushed it aside," he said.
Lemon-lime Sprite has become the fastest growing major soft drink brand in the United States with volume gains "in the high 20s," Coke has said.

"Coke has done a terrific job with Sprite, which is directed at Generation X. They have demonstrated that they can reach young people with the right product and message. We'll see how it's positioned. It's not actually so much an attack on the Mountain Dew share as an attempt to expand the category," said Martin Romm of CS First Boston.
But with Coke coming so late to the party, Mountain Dew has had a long lead making inroads in the category.
"It has been a little while in coming. But Coke has has other priorities. Mello Yello (a heavy citrus drink similar to Mountain Dew) was allowed to languish a bit," Pirko said.
